[P2] Anchor delays to when the operation is scheduled

An invocation can perform work before creating a wait or retry. For example, if a step takes ten seconds and then starts a five-second wait, this calculation targets invocation start plus five seconds—already in the past. The orchestrator marks the wait successful without advancing those five seconds. Retry delays after slow failures are shortened similarly, so local tests can observe completion earlier than the workflow permits. Carry each delay's creation time in the fake-clock domain and retain the original target for replayed waits. Add regression tests for a slow step followed by a wait and a retry after a slow failure; the new tests only create delays near invocation start.
